solve: Re-solved by T-3365 (2026-11-12) as a LEVEL CAMERA TURNED 22.4 DEGREES SOUTH OF SQUARE (yaw -67.64 in the footprint frame: u toward the street, v SOUTH on this side of the avenue), replacing T-1913's camera square to the front, because the print's level lines are not parallel: they converge on a vanishing point to the right, on the horizon. THE EVIDENCE. (1) The slope of the front's coursing, read in 80 windows across it (each window's courses and brick joints straightened by a sheared projection), is a straight line in the window's height, zero at y 1577 px and turning negative below it (the walk's lines rise to the right): slope = 0.000157 (1577 - y), 0.026 RMS. A wall that settled or a sheared print would not put the zero on the eye's own level; a turned camera must. (2) 2011 Prairie's flat front over the party line (x 1245 px) falls exactly as this vanishing point predicts (0.15, 0.10, 0.09, 0.08 against 0.14, 0.10, 0.09, 0.07), so the fall is not 2009's own; 2011's round tower reads level at its face, as a cylinder does. (3) The front's brick courses are 6.42 px apart beside the north corner (x 430-560) and 5.74 px beside the party line (x 1000-1130) at the same heights: through this camera 59-60 mm a course at both ends, through the square one 64 against 57 mm, which one wall cannot be. So the course at about 9.1 m and the paired light's hood, which T-3365's match record found falling to the south, are level (the course reads 9.1 m at both ends, the hood's top 11.3-11.4 m), and the square camera's uniform 100 px a metre read heights on the north side up to about 8% high. THE FIT. The front's two ends, the north corner's quoins (x 390 px) and the party line (x 1145 px), are the 1911 sheet's 7.56 m front, its foot y 1725 px at the north corner; the front's vanishing point x 7134 px (read at 7100 +/- 600 from the coursing); the north flank's vanishing point x 135 px (T-1913 read the flank's level lines meeting at 157.6); the eye 2.18 m north of the north wall (T-1913's 2.34, the place from which Monroe's plate hides the rear stack); and the stoop, which runs straight out from the door between its cheek walls: at x 940 and 1105 px at the house and 1095 and 1300 px at its foot, its foot taken 4.5 m out (the build's twelve risers on 0.3 m treads and a 1.2 m landing), fitted to 7 and 6 px. The eye stands 1.37 m over the wall's foot, about 21.9 m in front of the front's middle; principal point x 1147.8, y 1577 px (the horizon); f 2461.8 px. A metre on the front is 112 px across and 108 px up at the north corner, 102 px up at the middle and 96 px up at the party line (the square camera: 100 px everywhere). WHAT IS SOFT: the stoop's length sets the scale's absolute level: taken at 4.0 m the middle reads 103 px a metre up, at 5.0 m 100 px, every reading within 7 px either way; so a height read off the middle of the front carries about 2% in its absolute level, while its fall from north to south (12% across the front) does not. LIGHT: a grey sky, no cast shadows on the front: overcast.
